52 void screen_init(Screen *s) {
53 s->head = s->tail = s->cursor = make_line();
54 s->cursor_col = 0;
55 }
56
57 void screen_clear(Screen *s) {
58 Line *line = s->head;
59 while (line) {
60 Line *next = line->next;
61 free(line->data);
62 free(line);
63 line = next;
64 }
65 screen_init(s);
66 }
67
68 void screen_newline(Screen *s) {
69 if (s->cursor->next == NULL) {
70 Line *new_line = make_line();
71 s->cursor->next = new_line;
72 s->tail = new_line;
73 }
74 s->cursor = s->cursor->next;
75 s->cursor_col = 0;
76 }
77
78 void screen_cursor_up(Screen *s) {
79 if (s->cursor == s->head) return;
80 Line *line = s->head;
81 while (line && line->next != s->cursor) line = line->next;
82 if (line) s->cursor = line;
83 }
84
85 void screen_cursor_to_home(Screen *s) {
86 s->cursor = s->head;
87 s->cursor_col = 0;
88 }
89
90 void screen_cursor_to_bol(Screen *s) {
91 s->cursor_col = 0;
92 }

94 void screen_putc(Screen *s, char c) {
95 if (c == '\n') {
96 screen_newline(s);
97 return;
98 }
99 if (s->cursor_col >= MAX_COLS - 1) return;
100 s->cursor->data[s->cursor_col++] = c;

103 void handle_escape_sequence(Screen *s, FILE *in, char first_char) {
104 if (first_char == '[') {
105 char buf[8] = {0};
106 int i = 0;
107 while (i < 7) {
108 int c = fgetc(in);
109 if (c == EOF) break;
110 buf[i++] = c;
111 if ((c >= '@' && c <= '~')) break; // CSI end
112 }
113 buf[i] = '\0';
114
115 if (strcmp(buf, "1A") == 0) {
116 screen_cursor_up(s);
117 } else if (strcmp(buf, "2J") == 0) {
118 screen_clear(s);
119 } else if (strcmp(buf, "2K") == 0) {
120 memset(s->cursor->data, 0, MAX_COLS);
121 } else if (strcmp(buf, "3J") == 0) {
122 screen_clear(s);
123 } else if (strcmp(buf, "F") == 0) {
124 screen_cursor_up(s);
125 screen_cursor_to_bol(s);
126 } else if (strcmp(buf, "G") == 0) {
127 screen_cursor_to_bol(s);
128 } else if (strcmp(buf, "H") == 0) {
129 screen_cursor_to_home(s);
130 } else {
131 // unknown sequence: print it raw
132 screen_putc(s, ESC);
133 screen_putc(s, '[');
134 for (int j = 0; j < i; j++)
135 screen_putc(s, buf[j]);
136 }
137 } else {
138 // unknown non-CSI sequence
139 screen_putc(s, ESC);
140 screen_putc(s, first_char);
141 }
142 }
143
144 void process_input(Screen *screen, FILE *in) {
145 int c;
146 while ((c = fgetc(in)) != EOF) {
147 if (c == ESC) {
148 int next = fgetc(in);
149 if (next == EOF) break;
150 handle_escape_sequence(screen, in, next);
151 } else {
152 screen_putc(screen, c);
153 }
154 }
155 }
156
157 void dump_output(Screen *s, FILE *out) {
158 for (Line *line = s->head; line != NULL; line = line->next)
159 fprintf(out, "%s\n", line->data);
160 }
161
162 int main(int argc, char **argv) {
163 FILE *in = stdin;
164 FILE *out = stdout;
165 char *outfile = NULL;
166
167 // CLI parsing
168 for (int i = 1; i < argc; i++) {
169 if (!strcmp(argv[i], "-o")) {
170 if (++i >= argc) die("Missing argument for -o\n");
171 outfile = argv[i];
172 } else if (!in || in == stdin) {
173 in = fopen(argv[i], "r");
174 if (!in) die("Failed to open %s\n", argv[i]);
175 }
176 }
177
178 if (outfile) {
179 out = fopen(outfile, "w");
180 if (!out) die("Failed to open %s for writing\n", outfile);
181 }
182
183 Screen screen;
184 screen_init(&screen);
185 process_input(&screen, in);
186 dump_output(&screen, out);
187
188 // cleanup
189 if (in && in != stdin) fclose(in);
190 if (out && out != stdout) fclose(out);
191 screen_clear(&screen);
192 return 0;
193 }

434 #define PY_SSIZE_T_CLEAN
435 #include <Python.h>
436
437 #define TERMDUMP_LIB
438 #include "termdump.c"
439
440 static PyObject* pytermdump_termdump(PyObject *self, PyObject *args) {
441 Py_buffer buffer;
442 PyObject *result = NULL;
443 char *processed_data;
444 size_t processed_len;
445
446 /* Parse the bytes/buffer object */
447 if (!PyArg_ParseTuple(args, "y*", &buffer)) {
448 return NULL;
449 }
450
451 /* Process the buffer */
452 processed_data = process_buffer((const unsigned char*)buffer.buf, buffer.len, &processed_len);
453 if (!processed_data) {
454 PyErr_SetString(PyExc_MemoryError, "Failed to allocate memory for result");
455 PyBuffer_Release(&buffer);
456 return NULL;
457 }
458
459 /* Create a new bytes object with the processed data */
460 result = PyBytes_FromStringAndSize(processed_data, processed_len);
461
462 /* Clean up */
463 free(processed_data);
464 PyBuffer_Release(&buffer);
465
466 return result;
467 }
468
469 /* Module method definitions */
470 static PyMethodDef PytermdumpMethods[] = {
471 {"termdump", pytermdump_termdump, METH_VARARGS, "Process terminal escape sequences in a buffer."},
472 {NULL, NULL, 0, NULL} /* Sentinel */
473 };
474
475 /* Module definition */
476 static struct PyModuleDef pytermdumpmodule = {
477 PyModuleDef_HEAD_INIT,
478 "pytermdump", /* name of module */
479 "Python wrapper for termdump utility", /* module documentation */
480 -1, /* size of per-interpreter state (-1 = in global vars) */
481 PytermdumpMethods
482 };
483
484 /* Module initialization function */
485 PyMODINIT_FUNC PyInit_pytermdump(void) {
486 return PyModule_Create(&pytermdumpmodule);
487 }

549 1 # Claude Logging
550 1 # PyTermdump
551 2
552 3 Automatically keep logs of "claude code" sessions, and convert them to HTML.
553 3 A Python extension module that wraps the termdump C library for processing terminal escape sequences.
554 4
555 5 ## Features
556 6
557 7 - Processes ANSI escape sequences in terminal output
558 8 - Strips control characters and preserves text formatting
559 9 - Converts terminal output to styled HTML
560 10 - Supports syntax highlighting, bold text, and colors
561 11 - Includes line numbering and theme toggling in the HTML output
562 12
563 5 ## Installation
564 6
565 7 ```bash
566 8 pip install claude-logging
567 7 ```
568 8 pip install .
569 9 ```
570 10
571 11 ## Usage
572 12
573 13 ## License
574 13 ```python
575 14 import pytermdump
576 15
577 16 MIT License
578 16 # Process terminal escape sequences in a bytes object
579 17 input_data = b"\x1b[2JHello\x1b[1AWorld"
580 18 output_data = pytermdump.termdump(input_data)
581 19 print(output_data.decode('utf-8'))
582 20 ```
583 21
584 22 ## Features
585 23
586 24 - Process ANSI/VT100 terminal escape sequences
587 25 - Works with any object supporting the buffer protocol (bytes, bytearray, etc.)
588 26 - Returns processed output as bytes object with escape sequences handled appropriately

1744 import re
1745 import sys
1746 import argparse
1747 from html import escape
1748
1749
1750 # ANSI color codes
1751 RESET = 0
1752 BOLD = 1
1753 FG_BLACK = 30
1754 FG_RED = 31
1755 FG_GREEN = 32
1756 FG_YELLOW = 33
1757 FG_BLUE = 34
1758 FG_MAGENTA = 35
1759 FG_CYAN = 36
1760 FG_WHITE = 37
1761 BG_BLACK = 40
1762 BG_RED = 41
1763 BG_GREEN = 42
1764 BG_YELLOW = 43
1765 BG_BLUE = 44
1766 BG_MAGENTA = 45
1767 BG_CYAN = 46
1768 BG_WHITE = 47
1769
1770 # True color indicators
1771 FG_TRUE_COLOR = 38
1772 BG_TRUE_COLOR = 48
1773
1774 # Regular expression to find ANSI escape sequences
1775 ANSI_ESCAPE_RE = re.compile(r'\x1b\[((?:\d+;)*\d*)m')
1776
1777
1778 def parse_ansi_code(code_str):
1779 """Parse ANSI code into a list of integers."""
1780 if not code_str:
1781 return [0] # Default to reset
1782 return [int(c) for c in code_str.split(';') if c]
1783
1784
1785 def ansi_to_css(ansi_codes):
1786 """Convert ANSI codes to CSS styles."""
1787 styles = []
1788 fg_color = None
1789 bg_color = None
1790 bold = False
1791
1792 i = 0
1793 while i < len(ansi_codes):
1794 code = ansi_codes[i]
1795
1796 if code == RESET:
1797 return [] # Reset all styles
1798 elif code == BOLD:
1799 bold = True
1800 # Handle true color (24-bit) foreground: ESC[38;2;r;g;bm
1801 elif code == FG_TRUE_COLOR and i + 4 < len(ansi_codes) and ansi_codes[i+1] == 2:
1802 r, g, b = ansi_codes[i+2], ansi_codes[i+3], ansi_codes[i+4]
1803 styles.append(f"fg-true-color")
1804 styles.append(f"fg-rgb-{r}-{g}-{b}")
1805 i += 4 # Skip the parameters we just processed
1806 # Handle true color (24-bit) background: ESC[48;2;r;g;bm
1807 elif code == BG_TRUE_COLOR and i + 4 < len(ansi_codes) and ansi_codes[i+1] == 2:
1808 r, g, b = ansi_codes[i+2], ansi_codes[i+3], ansi_codes[i+4]
1809 styles.append(f"bg-true-color")
1810 styles.append(f"bg-rgb-{r}-{g}-{b}")
1811 i += 4 # Skip the parameters we just processed
1812 # Handle standard foreground colors
1813 elif FG_BLACK <= code <= FG_WHITE:
1814 fg_color = code - FG_BLACK
1815 styles.append(f"c{fg_color}")
1816 # Handle standard background colors
1817 elif BG_BLACK <= code <= BG_WHITE:
1818 bg_color = code - BG_BLACK
1819 styles.append(f"bg{bg_color}")
1820
1821 i += 1
1822
1823 if bold:
1824 styles.append("bold")
1825
1826 return styles
1827
1828
1829 def ansi_to_html(text):
1830 """Convert ANSI colored text to HTML with CSS classes."""
1831 result = []
1832 pos = 0
1833 active_styles = []
1834
1835 # Process all ANSI escape sequences
1836 for match in ANSI_ESCAPE_RE.finditer(text):
1837 # Add text before the escape sequence
1838 if pos < match.start():
1839 if active_styles:
1840 css_class = " ".join(active_styles)
1841 result.append(f'<span class="{css_class}">{escape(text[pos:match.start()])}</span>')
1842 else:
1843 result.append(escape(text[pos:match.start()]))
1844
1845 # Process the escape sequence
1846 ansi_codes = parse_ansi_code(match.group(1))
1847 if 0 in ansi_codes: # Reset
1848 active_styles = []
1849 else:
1850 active_styles = ansi_to_css(ansi_codes)
1851
1852 pos = match.end()
1853
1854 # Add any remaining text
1855 if pos < len(text):
1856 if active_styles:
1857 css_class = " ".join(active_styles)
1858 result.append(f'<span class="{css_class}">{escape(text[pos:])}</span>')
1859 else:
1860 result.append(escape(text[pos:]))
1861
1862 return ''.join(result)
1863
1864
1865 def generate_html(input_text):
1866 """Generate complete HTML with the converted content."""
1867 lines = input_text.split('\n')
1868 html_lines = []
1869
1870 for i, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
1871 html_content = ansi_to_html(line)
1872 html_lines.append(
1873 f'<div id="L{i}" class="line" data-line-number="{i}">'
1874 f'<span class="line-number">{i}</span>'
1875 f'<span class="line-content">{html_content}</span>'
1876 f'</div>'
1877 )
1878
1879 html_content = '\n'.join(html_lines)
1880

2153 // Handle initial hash (permalink)
2154 function handlePermalink() {{
2155 const hash = window.location.hash;
2156 if (!hash) return;
2157
2158 if (hash.includes('-')) {{
2159 const [start, end] = hash.slice(1).split('-').map(id => parseInt(id.slice(1)));
2160 if (!isNaN(start) && !isNaN(end)) {{
2161 clearHighlights();
2162 highlightRange(start, end);
2163 firstSelectedLine = null;
2164 }}
2165 }} else {{
2166 const lineNum = parseInt(hash.slice(2));
2167 if (!isNaN(lineNum)) {{
2168 clearHighlights();
2169 highlightLine(lineNum);
2170 firstSelectedLine = lineNum;
2171 }}
2172 }}
2173 }}
2174
2175 // Handle permalink on page load and when hash changes
2176 window.addEventListener('hashchange', handlePermalink);
2177 document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', () => {{
2178 handlePermalink();
2179 processRgbColors();
2180 }});
2181
2182 // Process colors immediately
2183 processRgbColors();
2184 </script>
2185 </body>
2186 </html>'''

2688 static PyObject* pytermdump_termdump(PyObject *self, PyObject *args) {
2689 Py_buffer buffer;
2690 PyObject *result = NULL;
2691 char *processed_data;
2692 size_t processed_len;
2693
2694 /* Parse the bytes/buffer object */
2695 if (!PyArg_ParseTuple(args, "y*", &buffer)) {
2696 return NULL;
2697 }
2698
2699 /* Process the buffer */
2700 processed_data = process_buffer((const unsigned char*)buffer.buf, buffer.len, &processed_len);
2701 if (!processed_data) {
2702 PyErr_SetString(PyExc_MemoryError, "Failed to allocate memory for result");
2703 PyBuffer_Release(&buffer);
2704 return NULL;
2705 }
2706
2707 /* Create a new bytes object with the processed data */
2708 result = PyBytes_FromStringAndSize(processed_data, processed_len);
2709
2710 /* Clean up */
2711 free(processed_data);
2712 PyBuffer_Release(&buffer);
2713
2714 return result;
2715 }

3076● Let's add a README.md file with usage information for the project:

3080 # Claude Logging
3081
3082 A utility for processing Claude AI log files with terminal control sequences (ANSI escape codes)
3083 and converting them to readable HTML files.
3084
3085 ## Features
3086
3087 - Processes ANSI escape sequences in terminal output
3088 - Strips control characters and preserves text formatting
3089 - Converts terminal output to styled HTML
3090 - Supports syntax highlighting, bold text, and colors
3091 - Includes line numbering and theme toggling in the HTML output
3092
3093 ## Installation
3094
3095 ```bash
3096 pip install claude-logging
3097 ```
3098
3099 ## Usage
3100
3101 ### Command Line
3102
3103 ```bash
3104 # Basic usage - converts input.log to input.html in the current directory
3105 claude-logging dump input.log
3106
3107 # Specify an output file
3108 claude-logging dump input.log -o output.html
3109
3110 # Process from stdin
3111 cat input.log | claude-logging dump - -o output.html
3112 ```
3113
3114 ### Python API
3115
3116 ```python
3117 from claude_logging import pytermdump
3118 from claude_logging.ansi2html import generate_html
3119
3120 # Process terminal escape sequences
3121 with open('input.log', 'rb') as f:
3122 input_data = f.read()
3123
3124 processed_data = pytermdump.termdump(input_data)
3125 processed_text = processed_data.decode('utf-8', errors='replace')
3126
3127 # Convert to HTML
3128 html_output = generate_html(processed_text)
3129
3130 # Save to file
3131 with open('output.html', 'w') as f:
3132 f.write(html_output)
3133 ```
3134
3135 ## HTML Output Features
3136
3137 - Clean, readable output with preserved formatting
3138 - Line numbers for easy reference
3139 - Dark and light theme toggle
3140 - Clickable lines for permalinks
3141 - Support for all terminal colors and formatting
3142
3143 ## Building from Source
3144
3145 ```bash
3146 # Clone the repository
3147 git clone https://github.com/yourusername/claude-logging.git
3148 cd claude-logging
3149
3150 # Install in development mode
3151 pip install -e .
3152 ```
3153
3154 ## License
3155
3156 MIT License

3408● Read(file_path: "/home/antocuni/pypy/misc/claude-logging/claude-logging-2/claude_logging/pytermdump.c")…
3409  ⎿  #define PY_SSIZE_T_CLEAN
3410 #include <Python.h>
3411
3412 // No need to define TERMDUMP_LIB anymore since it's the default behavior
3413 #include "termdump.c"
3414
3415 static PyObject* pytermdump_termdump(PyObject *self, PyObject *args) {
3416 Py_buffer buffer;
3417 PyObject *result = NULL;
3418 char *processed_data;
3419 size_t processed_len;
3420
3421 /* Parse the bytes/buffer object */
3422 if (!PyArg_ParseTuple(args, "y*", &buffer)) {
3423 return NULL;
3424 }
3425
3426 /* Process the buffer */
3427 processed_data = process_buffer((const unsigned char*)buffer.buf, buffer.len, &processed_len);
3428 if (!processed_data) {
3429 PyErr_SetString(PyExc_MemoryError, "Failed to allocate memory for result");
3430 PyBuffer_Release(&buffer);
3431 return NULL;
3432 }
3433
3434 /* Create a new bytes object with the processed data */
3435 result = PyBytes_FromStringAndSize(processed_data, processed_len);
3436
3437 /* Clean up */
3438 free(processed_data);
3439 PyBuffer_Release(&buffer);
3440
3441 return result;
3442 }
3443
3444 /* Module method definitions */
3445 static PyMethodDef PytermdumpMethods[] = {
3446 {"termdump", pytermdump_termdump, METH_VARARGS, "Process terminal escape sequences in a buffer."},
3447 {NULL, NULL, 0, NULL} /* Sentinel */
3448 };
3449
3450 /* Module definition */
3451 static struct PyModuleDef pytermdumpmodule = {
3452 PyModuleDef_HEAD_INIT,
3453 "claude_logging.pytermdump", /* name of module */
3454 "Python wrapper for termdump utility", /* module documentation */
3455 -1, /* size of per-interpreter state (-1 = in global vars) */
3456 PytermdumpMethods
3457 };
3458
3459 /* Module initialization function */
3460 PyMODINIT_FUNC PyInit_pytermdump(void) {
3461 return PyModule_Create(&pytermdumpmodule);
3462 }

3631● Now our package is configured to:
3632
3633 1. Use the Python stable ABI (limited API) starting from Python 3.8
3634 2. Build a universal wheel that works across multiple Python versions (3.8+)
3635 3. Have a GitHub Action workflow that builds for multiple platforms (Linux, Windows, macOS)
3636 4. Publish to PyPI automatically when a release is created
3637
3638 The stable ABI approach dramatically simplifies the build process since we only need to build one wheel per platform, rather than one for each Python version.

3900 This command will:
3901 - Create a release tagged as v0.1.0
